If yes, enter the eight-digit Scheme Reference Number (SRN).

If you have disclosed a tax avoidance scheme under the DOTAS rules, HMRC will have given you an 8 digit-long Scheme Reference Number (SRN).

Enter this number.

This field is conditional mandatory.

6.2 Employing company

Enter the details of the company that employs the employee who was awarded or acquired the ERS.

Refer to the technical note for mandatory fields.

6.3 Employee first name

This is the employee’s first name.

This field is mandatory.

6.4 Employee second name (optional).

If the employee has a second name, then enter in this column.

This field is optional.

6.5 Employee last name

This is the employee’s last name.

This field is mandatory.

6.6 National Insurance number

Enter in the correct format, for example, QQ123456C

Most individuals included on an ERS end of year return will have a National Insurance number.

In exceptional cases, use an alternative reference instead.

This reference must:

only be used on the ERS end of year return

not be used in any other HMRC correspondence

not be given to the individual

Where there are exceptional circumstances, the required format for the alternative ERS reference will be a total of 9 characters. This will be 2 letters, 6 numbers and one letter consisting of:

TN – to indicate an ERS reference

Employee Date of Birth in format DDMMYY (for example, 080403) ― this data will enable HMRC to trace the individual

No National Insurance number Reason Identifier (X, Y or Z) ― this is to identify the reason why an individual does not have a National Insurance number

X ― Under 16 years old

Y ― Applied for a National Insurance number and is waiting to receive it

Z — Never paid National Insurance contributions as they have not been liable to UK National Insurance contributions ― for example, they’re not resident in the UK or are an ‘intra-company worker’ on transfer to work in the UK

This field is mandatory.

6.7 Company Registration Number (CRN)

This is the number issued by Companies House to UK registered companies. If the company is not UK registered or does not have this number, then do not make any entry in this column.

This field is optional.

6.8 Recognised stock exchange

For more information, go to Recognised stock exchanges .

AIM and PISCES are not recognised stock exchanges for these purposes.

6.9 Has a NICs election or agreement been operated?

This is when the employer and the employee agree or jointly elect for the employee to meet the employer’s liability to pay secondary National Insurance contributions on certain types of share awards and share options gains. The employee can then get a deduction equal to the amount of secondary or employers’ National Insurance contributions transferred when working out the amount chargeable to Income Tax. ‘Operated’ means when the secondary or employers’ National Insurance contributions is recovered under the terms of election or agreement already made between the employer and the employee.

This field is mandatory.

6.10 Was PAYE operated?

Enter ‘yes’ or ‘no’ in this field.

If shares are readily convertible into cash and a reportable event is taxable such as an acquisition of the shares, then PAYE should have been operated to collect any Income Tax and NICs due.

There are exceptions, for example, following death (check ERSM20270 - Employment-related securities and options: exclusions: deaths), or after an employee leaves and the 7-year rule applies (check ERSM20280 - Employment-related securities and options: exclusions: 7 year rule).

This field is mandatory.

6.11 Was any adjustment made for amounts subject to apportionment for residence or duties outside the UK?

Where the employee is an ‘internationally mobile employee’ (IME), the income derived from the securities may be apportioned if the required conditions are met. The rules for IMEs will identify any foreign securities income which is either not chargeable to UK Income Tax or taxable only when remitted to the UK. Guidance on the ERS rules for IMEs can be found at ERSM162000 - International from 6 April 2015 and ERSM165000 - International from 6 April 2025.

For further information regarding non-UK domiciled individuals see UK tax residence guidance.

This field is mandatory.

7. Worksheet specific guidance

The following sections explain when to use each worksheet and how to complete its questions.

Use a separate row for each individual unless stated otherwise.

(All worksheet definitions, questions, routing rules, thresholds, examples and calculations remain unchanged and are presented in a clearer sequence below.)

Please note when completing the end of year return if you leave 10 or more consecutive rows blank with no data populated, it will be assumed that there is no further information contained below these blank rows within the sheet. Therefore, it is important you do not leave blank rows between the rows of data you are reporting. Note the system will continue to check for information on subsequent sheets within the same end of year return.

8. Non‑TASS_Grants_V7_worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about any employment related securities options granted in the tax year.

Include all types of securities options including nil cost options. Reporting of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) will depend on how these are structured. Whether the RSUs are considered securities options or not will determine on which worksheet these should be reported.

For more information read securities options guidance.

8.1 Question 1: Date of grant

Enter the date the ERS options were granted to the employees.

Use the format yyyy‑mm‑dd (for example: 2023‑10‑31).

The date of grant will be on the option certificate, and it must fall within the tax year covered by this return.

This field is optional.

13.8 Questions 13 to 15

See common fields guidance in section 6.

14 Non‑TASS_Notional_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about the amount of notional loan outstanding immediately before discharge for each relevant person in the tax year.

You must fill in this sheet where a notional loan is treated as discharged, creating a taxable amount. This may occur when the employment related securities are disposed of to someone other than to a connected person, or an outstanding liability to pay for the securities is released.

When a notional loan is discharged, the resulting amount is treated as employment income and is subject to Income Tax.

Where the securities are readily convertible assets, the amount is subject to Income Tax and National Insurance contributions and must be accounted for through PAYE.

Use a separate row for each individual.

14.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date the notional loan was treated as discharged.

This field is mandatory.

14.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

14.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

14.4 Question 9: Date securities were originally acquired

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy‑mm‑dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date the securities were originally acquired, even if you are reporting a later event.

This field is mandatory.

14.5 Question 10: Number of securities originally acquired

Enter the number of securities to 2 decimal places. For example: 100.00.

Enter the number, not the value, of securities originally acquired on which the discharge of the notional loan occurred.

This field is optional.

14.6 Question 11: Amount of notional loan discharged

Enter the value in pounds sterling to 4 decimal places. For example: 10.1234.

Enter the amount of the notional loan outstanding immediately before discharge.

This field is optional.

14.7 Questions 12 to 13

See common fields guidance in section 6.

15 Non‑TASS_Enhancement_V7 worksheet

You must use this worksheet to tell HMRC about any securities artificially enhanced.

For example, the market value of an employee’s employment related securities is increased by more than 10% by non-commercial actions in a relevant period. The relevant period runs from the date securities are acquired to the earlier of the date of disposal or 5 April of the tax year for this reportable event. The date of the taxable event will be 5 April or the date the securities were disposed of, if earlier.

Use a different row to report each individual’s details.

15.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

This is the date of the taxable event and will be 5 April or the date the securities were disposed of if earlier.

This field is mandatory.

15.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

15.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

15.4 Question 9: Date securities originally acquired

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy‑mm‑dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date the securities on which you are reporting an enhancement event were originally acquired.

This field is mandatory.

15.5 Question 10: Number of securities originally acquired

Enter the number to 2 decimal places. For example: 100.00.

Enter the number, not the value, of securities originally acquired.

This field is optional.

15.6 Question 11: Total Unrestricted Market Value (UMV) on 5th April or date of disposal if earlier.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places. For example, 10.1234.

Enter the total UMV on 5 April or date of disposal of securities if earlier. This is the market value of the securities ignoring the effect of restrictions, any artificial reduction, or in relation to convertible securities the market value excluding the right to convert.

This field is optional.

15.7 Question 12: Total UMV ignoring effect of artificial increase on date of taxable event.

Enter the value in pounds to 4 decimal places. For example: 10.1234.

This value should be calculated on the same basis as Question 11:

Enter the total UMV on 5 April or date of disposal of securities if earlier. This is the market value of the securities ignoring the effect of restrictions, any artificial reduction, or in relation to convertible securities the market value excluding the right to convert.

This field is optional.

15.8 Questions 13 to 14

See common fields guidance in section 6.

16 Non‑TASS_Sold_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC about securities sold for more than their market value for each relevant person in the tax year.

This worksheet should be completed if the employee, or a person connected with the employee, has disposed of employment related securities on or after the 6 April for more than their market value at the time of disposal.

In these circumstances, the amount treated as employment income is the consideration received on disposal, less the market value of the securities at disposal, and any allowable expenses.

Use a different row to report each individual’s details.

16.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd). For example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter date securities were sold for more than their market value.

This field is mandatory.

16.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

there were artificial reductions (not discounts) in the market value of securities arising from non-commercial actions. Checkexamples in: ERSM50030 - Securities with Artificially Depressed Value.

Non-commercial actions include any reduction made:

for anything other than a genuine commercial purpose

as part of a scheme or arrangement designed to avoid tax or National Insurance contributions

because of any transaction between companies within a group on preferential terms that would not have been made if the companies were at arm’s length

This field is mandatory.

10.23 Question 36: If there was an artificial reduction in value, nature of the artificial reduction.

Only complete this if you answered ‘yes’ to Question 35.

Enter a number from 1 to 3:

Non-commercial transaction.

Scheme or arrangement designed to avoid tax or National Insurance.

Inter- company transaction on a non-arm’s length basis.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.24 Question 37: Were shares acquired under an employee shareholder arrangement?

Enter yes or no.

You should only make an entry in this column if shares were acquired under an Employee Shareholder agreement as defined in Section 205A of the Employment Rights Act 1996.

An employee shareholder is someone who works under an employee shareholder employment contract. Employees with an employee shareholder agreement have different employment rights to other employees.

As part of the agreement employee shareholders must be given shares worth at least £2000 on receipt.

This field is mandatory.

10.25 Question 38: If shares were acquired under an employee shareholder arrangement, was the total actual market value (AMV) of shares £2,000 or more?

Enter yes or no.

Enter yes if the AMV of the shares acquired under an employee shareholder arrangement is £2,000 or more.

This field is conditional mandatory.

10.26 Question 39 and 40

See common fields guidance in section 6.

11 Non‑TASS_RestrictedSecurities_V7 worksheet

Use this worksheet to tell HMRC details of chargeable events after acquisition of restricted securities.

Securities are considered restricted securities if their market value is reduced because of restrictions, such as those relating to transfer, reversion or forfeiture. The chargeable amount is calculated using a prescribed formula.

You can get a spreadsheet to help you determine this amount by emailing, shareschemes@hmrc.gov.uk.

When chargeable events arise

A chargeable event arises if:

the securities stop being subject to forfeiture (conditional)

any restriction is changed or removed from the securities by any means, including if any time restrictions have lapsed

the securities are sold to an unconnected person while still restricted

Use a separate row for each individual.

11.1 Question 1: Date of event

Enter the date in the correct format (yyyy-mm-dd), for example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter date of reportable events occurring after acquisition of restricted securities.

This field is mandatory.

11.2 Questions 2 to 7

See common fields guidance in section 6.

11.3 Question 8: PAYE reference of employing company

Enter the PAYE reference number of the company that employs the employee.

The employing company should be the company with the PAYE obligation.

This field is mandatory.

11.4 Question 9: Date securities originally acquired.

Enter the date in the format (yyyy‑mm‑dd), for example: 2023‑10‑31.

This is the date when the restricted securities on which you are now reporting an event were originally acquired.

This field is mandatory.

11.5 Question 10: Number of securities originally acquired

Enter the number of securities to 2 decimal places (for example: 100.00).

Enter the number, not the value, of restricted securities originally acquired.

This field is optional.

11.6 Question 11: For disposals or lifting of restrictions, total chargeable amount.

Enter the amount in pounds to 4 decimal places (for example: 10.1234).

Enter the total amount chargeable when restrictions on securities are lifted or there is a disposal of restricted securities.

For the vesting of restricted securities, the chargeable amount in box 11 should be based on the value of the gross number of shares subject to the chargeable event.

This applies even if some shares are disposed of at the time to cover Income Tax and National Insurance contributions.

This field is optional.

11.7 Question 12: For lifting of restrictions, are the shares listed on a recognised stock exchange?

Enter yes or no.

If yes, go to question 15.

If no, go to question 13.

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.8 Question 13: If the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange, was a valuation agreed with HMRC?

Enter yes or no.

Only complete this question if the shares were not listed on a recognised stock exchange.

If yes, go to question 14.

If no, go to question 15.

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.9 Question 14: If yes, enter the HMRC valuation reference given.

Enter the HMRC valuation reference, this will be on the valuation letter sent to you from the Shares and Assets Valuation office. The reference given will normally be your Company Reference Number (CRN).

Enter the full reference including the letters and numbers.

If it begins with 3 letters, enter numbers only.

This field is conditional mandatory.

11.10 Question 15: For variations, date of variation.

Enter the date in the format (yyyy‑mm‑dd) for example: 2023‑10‑31.

Enter the date when there has been an increase in value of the securities because of alteration in the rights or any restrictions attached to them or other shares in the company.

Do not complete this column in connection with the variation if:

all of the shares of the same class are similarly restricted

the majority of the shares are held by persons other than employees or directors

employees or directors control the company by virtue of their holdings of that class of shares
